classification.difficultyReason: Sketch familiar curves, recognise symmetry and use doubled definite integrals to calculate geometric area.

content.prompt: Sketch the curve and look carefully for any symmetries that will simplify the calculation. Find the area of the region bounded by the given curve and the $y$-axis.

answer.worked:
$x=2y$ is odd in $y$. The curve lies to the right of the $y$-axis for $0<y<5$ and to the left for $-5<y<0$. The two regions have equal area by symmetry about the origin.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\int_0^5 2y\,dy\\&=2\left[y^2\right]_0^5\\&=2(25-0)\\&=50\text{ u}^2.\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
$x=y^2\ge0$, so the curve lies on or to the right of the $y$-axis. Since $y^2$ is even in $y$, the graph is symmetric about the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\int_0^3 y^2\,dy\\&=2\left[\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^3\\&=2(9-0)\\&=18\text{ u}^2.\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $y=\pm2$ and lies to its right for $-2<y<2$. Since $4-y^2$ is even in $y$, the graph is symmetric about the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\int_0^2(4-y^2)\,dy\\&=2\left[4y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2\\&=2\left(8-\frac83\right)\\&=\frac{32}{3}\text{ u}^2.\end{align*}$$
